phase: 1 — lazy min-heap top-K (replaces the O(C·log C) full sort)

hardware.note: mobile CPU, thermal-throttled, single-thread; HIGH run-to-run variance (see qps_std) — absolute numbers understate a server

method: end-to-end query latency for ORDER BY embedding <-> q LIMIT 10, 8 runs (mean±std over per-run mean latency, best-of-8 for qps_best), 200 queries seed 7; baseline = theo-db:m35 (full sort), optimized = theo-db:m36 (lazy heap); IDENTICAL data/index/probes/k on both. The two images differ by EXACTLY one engine commit (8e2bdab, am/scan.rs only) since v0.32.0 — verified via `git diff 37c9765..8e2bdab -- '*.rs'`.
recall: IDENTICAL by construction — `Scored` orders by (f64::total_cmp, tid), the exact total order the old `results.sort_by((partial_cmp, tid))` produced on finite L2 distances, so the emitted top-K is byte-identical. Proven by the `heap_pops_same_order_as_sort_with_ties` pg_test + the full 61-test suite passing unchanged (kNN-id-comparison subset returns the same ids; the suite also includes negative/privilege tests). The latency driver itself does not diff ids.
measurement_first_finding: the M36 profiler (THEODB_SCAN_PROFILE) falsified the original 'quantize the distance' premise: distance is ~14-15% of scan cost; the bottlenecks are reads (~44-51%) and sort (~35-41%). Phase 1 attacks sort.

profiler_sort_phase.note: amrescan-side phase, probes=50, cand=50332, THEODB_SCAN_PROFILE=1 — this is the STABLE, algorithmic finding (O(C·log C) full sort → O(C) heapify; the per-pop O(log C)×k moved to amgettuple, bounded by the executor LIMIT and unprofiled)

verdict.end_to_end_speedup: ~1.4-1.7× (mean over 8 runs) at IDENTICAL recall. HIGH variance on the throttled CPU — the per-probe ratio is not cleanly monotonic; treat it as a ~1.5× band, not a precise per-point number. Consistent with the Amdahl ceiling: sort is ~37-41% of scan, so removing it caps the scan speedup near ~1.5-1.7× — the measured mean sits at that ceiling (a small extra from the comparator + allocation change).
verdict.closes_scann_gap: partially — this attacks the ~35-41% sort phase only. The remaining ~44-51% reads phase is M36 Phase 2 (smaller quantized codes to cut I/O + f32 rerank). The full ScaNN gap (~25×, M33) also needs harder candidate pruning. HONEST: this is a real ~1.5× scan speedup at preserved recall, NOT '25× from the sort alone'.
honest_notes: The STABLE claim is the profiler's ~10-13× sort-phase reduction (algorithmic). The end-to-end ~1.5× is Amdahl-bounded and variance-heavy.

Blob (legacy M26) scan path: for exact-distance ties with an empty pending region, the tie-break normalizes from corpus-position to tid — a more-deterministic order, not a recall change; the byte-identical claim is exact on the structured (shipping) paths.

reproduction: for each of theo-db:m35 (sort) and theo-db:m36 (heap), same host: PGPORT=<port> python3 benchmarks/run_m36_scan.py --n 200000 --probes 50 --k 10 --runs 8 --label <sort|heap>
